correctness.rationale: At zero detuning the one-step product is bd; the scalar iterate has g(x)-x=x((b-A)x-bd)/(Ax+bd). Monotonicity of each orbit and the unique positive fixed point give the full stable line and both escape limits, including initial y=0. For small detuning the equilibrium has an eigenvalue near zero and an expanding eigenvalue near B/b. The forward local stable-manifold theorem with smooth parameter dependence applies also at the endomorphism parameter: the unstable block is invertible, and no inverse of the stable block is needed. The stable tangent has nonzero y component. Its one-step pullback has x derivative B/(A+y) on the unperturbed graph, uniformly positive on each prescribed compact. Local constructions can use slightly larger open intervals, including a small extension at y=0; the map is smooth there. For uniqueness even among eventual entrants, write the map in (x,-y) coordinates. It is strictly order preserving and the equilibrium derivative has positive entries and a positive left Perron vector for the expanding eigenvalue. In a convex neighborhood of the equilibrium the left-vector weighted gap of comparable points increases by a uniform factor greater than one, by integrating the derivative on their joining segment. Two distinct points with the same y and both converging would contradict this after entering the neighborhood. Joint smoothness with at least three parameter and two ordinate derivatives gives the compact C² remainder. Separate exact-symbolic substitution into the graph identity gave zero first- and second-order residuals, with u(q)=1/q and v(q)=0; differentiation gives v''=-2bq/[d B³(A+y)³]. This coefficient is bounded away from zero in magnitude on each compact, not along the full unbounded curve. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not run; its finite shooting is not evidence of global uniqueness or the compact-uniform remainder. The decisive symbolic calculation is replayable by expanding (d(A+y)+ε)/(s0+εu+ε²v) to order two and comparing the two sides of RESULT.md lines 72–96.

value.rationale: For a previously studied competitive system this resolves a specific geometric question not answered by a basin split: the first displacement is purely affine, but a nonzero quadratic effect bends the actual separator to the same side for either sign of detuning. The compact-uniform C² estimate makes that sign a conclusion about a true stable graph, rather than a formal curve or a few numerical examples.
